INTEGRATED SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM (TERM 1) 16
====

EXAM BODY: KJSEA
GRADE: Grade 8 JSS
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50

INSTRUCTIONS
----
• Answer all questions.
• For calculations, show full working (formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units).
• Diagrams provided are part of the question — use every labeled value.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In osmosis, what mainly moves across a selectively permeable membrane? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Sand grains
   C. Whole sugar crystals only
   D. Electric current

2. Eyepiece ×15 and objective ×40. What is total magnification? (1 mark)
   A. ×600
   B. ×55
   C. ×15
   D. ×80

3. The main energy chain in a simple torch is: (1 mark)
   A. Chemical → electrical → light (+ heat)
   B. Light → chemical → sound
   C. Sound → nuclear → light
   D. Heat → food → electricity only

4. Iron has symbol Fe from the Latin name: (1 mark)
   A. Ferrum
   B. Natrium
   C. Aurum
   D. Kalium

5. Which statement correctly defines an element? (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical or physical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A substance that always conducts electricity

6. A learner writes calcium as CA. What is the correct symbol and rule? (1 mark)
   A. Ca — first letter capital, second letter small
   B. CA — both letters must be capitals
   C. ca — both letters must be small
   D. C — calcium uses only one letter

7. Why is table salt (NaCl) classified as a compound? (1 mark)
   A. It contains sodium and chlorine chemically joined in a fixed ratio
   B. It is white and looks pure
   C. It melts when heated
   D. It is mined at Lake Magadi only

8. Which change is physical? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Baking soda reacting with vinegar to make a new gas

9. Which property of liquids is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Definite volume, no definite shape
   B. Definite shape and definite volume
   C. No definite volume and no mass
   D. Always denser than every solid

10. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread the burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

11. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction that forms a precipitate
   D. Heating a solid until it melts

12. In osmosis, what mainly moves across a selectively permeable membrane? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Sand grains
   C. Whole sugar crystals only
   D. Electric current

13. Eyepiece ×15 and objective ×40. What is total magnification? (1 mark)
   A. ×600
   B. ×55
   C. ×15
   D. ×80

14. Calculate pressure when F = 400 N and A = 0.2 m². (1 mark)
   A. 2000 Pa
   B. 80 Pa
   C. 400.2 Pa
   D. 0.0005 Pa

15. The main energy chain in a simple torch is: (1 mark)
   A. Chemical → electrical → light (+ heat)
   B. Light → chemical → sound
   C. Sound → nuclear → light
   D. Heat → food → electricity only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED QUESTIONS
----

19. Define osmosis and describe what happens to visking tubing with concentrated sugar solution in distilled water. (6 marks)

20. Trace the energy transformations in a torch from dry cells to the bulb. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. Correct option: A — Water

2. Correct option: A — ×600
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective
2. Substitute values: Total = 15 × 40
3. Total = 600
Final Answer: ×600
Marks: M1 multiply; A1 answer

3. Correct option: A — Chemical → electrical → light (+ heat)

4. Correct option: A — Ferrum

5. Correct option: A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical or physical means

6. Correct option: A — Ca — first letter capital, second letter small

7. Correct option: A — It contains sodium and chlorine chemically joined in a fixed ratio

8. Correct option: A — Ice melting to water

9. Correct option: A — Definite volume, no definite shape

10. Correct option: A — Water can spread the burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

11. Correct option: A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

12. Correct option: A — Water

13. Correct option: A — ×600
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective
2. Substitute values: Total = 15 × 40
3. Total = 600
Final Answer: ×600
Marks: M1 multiply; A1 answer

14. Correct option: A — 2000 Pa
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: P = F / A
2. Substitute values: P = 400 / 0.2
3. P = 2000
Final Answer: 2000 Pa
Marks: M1 substitute; A1 Pa

15. Correct option: A — Chemical → electrical → light (+ heat)

16. (6 marks)
Melting ice: still H₂O, no new substance, reversible by freezing → physical. Burning paper: ash/gases form, new substances, not simply reversible → chemical.

17. (8 marks)
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: P = F / A
2. Substitute values: P = 190 / 0.5
3. P = 380
Final Answer: 380 Pa
Marks: M1 formula/substitution; A1 final answer with Pa

18. (6 marks)
Fuel, heat, oxygen. For oil fires, do not use water; smother/cover to cut oxygen and get help / evacuate if needed.

19. (6 marks)
Osmosis: water moves across a selectively permeable membrane from dilute toward more concentrated solution. Water enters the tubing; it swells/gains mass.

20. (5 marks)
Chemical energy (cells) → electrical energy (circuit) → light energy + heat energy (bulb).
